page: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.E4.Flex.64-1024 is an x86_64 virtual instance configured with 64 physical cores and 128 vCPUs on dedicated AMD EPYC 7J13 processors running at 2.55 GHz. Cache hierarchy specifications include 64 KB of L1 data cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 16 MB of L3 cache. The platform provides 1024 GB of total system RAM, corresponding to 8.0 GB of memory per core. The instance includes zero GPUs and provides no bundled local storage, requiring network-attached storage for non-volatile file storage. A single complimentary public IPv4 address is assigned to the configuration.

Benchmark evaluations reveal substantial multi-threaded computational strength. In multi-core stress-ng tests and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression, the instance scores in the top tier. Cached memory bandwidth tests with small blocks reach the top 25% bracket, as do static web serving throughput and Redis operations, the latter exceeding 104 million operations per second. In contrast, single-core compute performance and single-threaded gzip compression remain in the middle tier, and large-block uncached memory read and write speeds also achieve average ranking.

The 1:8 core-to-memory ratio delivers qualitative efficiency for memory-constrained workloads without incurring the added costs of accelerated graphics hardware. The absence of integrated local storage necessitates network storage provisioning, which allows compute and persistence to scale independently. This server type fits memory-intensive enterprise tasks, large-scale in-memory databases, batch data pipelines, ETL workloads, and high-concurrency backend services.
description: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.E4.Flex.64-1024 is a memory-oriented virtual machine configuration powered by AMD EPYC 7J13 processors based on the x86_64 architecture. The instance provides 64 dedicated physical cores and 128 vCPUs clocked at 2.55 GHz, accompanied by 1024 GB of system memory, establishing an 8 GB per vCPU allocation. It contains no onboard GPUs and includes no local storage, requiring network-attached storage volumes for persistent data. Performance benchmarks indicate top-tier capabilities in multi-core CPU throughput and multi-threaded decompression, alongside strong caching throughput and high Redis transaction rates. However, single-core CPU throughput and large-block memory read/write bandwidth fall within the middle tier. With its substantial memory pool and massive parallel thread execution, this server is well configured for in-memory databases, large-scale ETL processing, containerized microservices, and memory-heavy distributed applications.
